introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Duration: One and Three Quarter Hours.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Study the following information about the market for rice produced by a non-governmental organisation (NGO) and answer the questions that follow.

| Price FCFA | Quantity demanded (000s kg) per week | Quantity supplied (000s kg) per week |
|---|---|---|
| 900 | 300 | 620 |
| 800 | 350 | 600 |
| 700 | 440 | 570 |
| 600 | 450 | 530 |
| 500 | 490 | 490 |
| 400 | 530 | 450 |
| 300 | 570 | 410 |

figures.legende: Demand and supply curves drawn from the schedule of the rice market, equilibrium E at 500 FCFA and 490 (000s kg), minimum price of 600 FCFA and the resulting surplus of 80 (000s kg) (model answer to Q2(b)).

incertitudes: Question 2(b)(i) : le sujet écrit « she » sans antécédent clair (le tableau parle d'une ONG, la mesure est prise par le gouvernement) ; le corrigé l'interprète comme le gouvernement ou l'organisme acheteur qui achète l'excédent.

Question 2 (tableau) : les écarts du tableau sont irréguliers (quantité demandée +10 seulement entre 700 et 600 FCFA, +50 ou +40 ailleurs ; offre +20, +30 puis +40) ; recopiés tels qu'imprimés, sans correction.
Question 2(b) : la figure est une figure du corrigé (matplotlib), tracée à partir du seul tableau du sujet ; le sujet n'impose aucun diagramme.
Question 2(b)(ii) : coût calculé comme excédent × prix minimum = 80 000 kg × 600 FCFA = 48 000 000 FCFA par semaine (vérifié avec Python).

La consigne « Answer ANY THREE questions » est exprimée par regles_choix (3 parmi 5). Aucun total par question n'est imprimé (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les `points` de chaque sous-question sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties, et la somme imprimée de la question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the equilibrium or market price and why? (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The equilibrium (market) price is **500 FCFA per kg** (1 mark for the price; 2 marks for the reason).

**Why:** at 500 FCFA the quantity demanded and the quantity supplied are equal, both **490 (000s kg) per week**, so the market clears: there is neither a surplus nor a shortage and no pressure for the price to change.

At any other price in the table the market is out of balance. For example, at 600 FCFA, $Q_s - Q_d = 530 - 450 = 80$ (000s kg) is a **surplus**, which pushes the price down; at 400 FCFA, $Q_d - Q_s = 530 - 450 = 80$ (000s kg) is a **shortage**, which pushes the price up. Only at 500 FCFA do the forces of demand and supply balance.

questions.enonce_markdown:
If the government imposes a minimum price of 600 FCFA per kg of rice,

(i) How many kilograms of rice will she have to buy to make sure that this policy works? (2 marks)

(ii) Calculate the total cost of the quantity implied in (b)(i) above to the government. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A minimum price of 600 FCFA is **above** the equilibrium price (500 FCFA), so it is effective and creates excess supply. The figure below shows the situation.

![fig-1](gce-al-economics-2025-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

**(i)** At 600 FCFA: quantity supplied = 530 (000s kg) and quantity demanded = 450 (000s kg).

$$\text{Surplus} = Q_s - Q_d = 530 - 450 = 80 \text{ (000s kg)} = 80\,000 \text{ kg per week}$$

To make the minimum price work, the government (or the buying agency) must **buy the surplus of 80 000 kg of rice per week**; otherwise the unsold rice would push the market price back down towards equilibrium.

**(ii)** The cost is the surplus bought at the minimum price:

$$\text{Cost} = 80\,000 \text{ kg} \times 600 \text{ FCFA per kg} = 48\,000\,000 \text{ FCFA}$$

The total cost to the government is **48 million FCFA per week** (that is, 48 000 thousand FCFA).

questions.enonce_markdown: List four negative consequences of the minimum price legislation. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four negative consequences (1 mark each, any four):

1. **Surplus (excess supply).** At the minimum price, producers supply more than consumers buy (80 000 kg a week in the table).
2. **Cost to the government and taxpayers.** Buying and storing the surplus is expensive and the money could have been used for other purposes (opportunity cost).
3. **Higher prices and lower consumption.** Consumers pay 600 FCFA instead of 500 FCFA and buy less (450 instead of 490 thousand kg), so consumer welfare falls, especially for poor households.
4. **Waste and storage problems.** Surplus rice must be stored, may deteriorate or be destroyed, or be dumped abroad.
5. **Resource misallocation.** The high price keeps inefficient producers in the industry and encourages over-production of rice instead of other goods.
6. **Black markets and evasion.** Sellers and buyers may trade illegally below the minimum price.

questions.enonce_markdown: State four factors that could lead to an increase in the demand for rice. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four factors (1 mark each, any four):

1. **An increase in consumers' income** (rice is a normal good).
2. **A rise in the price of a substitute** (for example maize, cassava or yam), so consumers switch to rice.
3. **A fall in the price of a complementary good** (for example cooking oil or tomatoes used with rice).
4. **A change in tastes and preferences in favour of rice**, for example through advertising or health campaigns.
5. **An increase in the size of the population** (more consumers).
6. **An expected future rise in the price of rice**, which makes consumers buy more now.

questions.enonce_markdown: Enumerate four factors that will make the supply of rice more elastic. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Four factors (1 mark each, any four):

1. **Time period.** The longer the time, the more elastic the supply, because farmers can plant and harvest more rice and firms can expand capacity.
2. **Spare capacity and unused resources.** Producers with idle land, labour or machines can raise output quickly when the price rises.
3. **Stocks.** Large stocks of stored rice can be released on to the market quickly.
4. **Mobility of factors of production.** If land, labour and capital can easily be switched from other crops or products to rice, supply responds more.
5. **Availability of inputs and low costs of increasing output** (seeds, fertiliser, credit, technology), and **freedom of entry** for new producers.
6. **Nature of the product.** A durable, storable product such as rice has a more elastic supply than a perishable one.
